Q20

The model's four 2022 houses spin one way (counter-clockwise from above); the drone photo shows them spinning the other way. Which is right — or is the model's map flipped left-to-right?

In the model each house sticks out past the end of the next one like the blades of a pinwheel, and seen from above that pinwheel turns counter-clockwise. In the 2022 drone photo (turned north-up from the heading the drone logged) the same four houses overlap the other way round, so it turns clockwise: that is a mirror image, which no turning of the map can fix.

Your answer

worth answering first What changes if you answer: If the photo is right, the 2022 layout is redrawn as its mirror image and the 2022 building replay is recorded again on it; if the model is right, nothing changes.

north-up: A photo turned so that north points to the top of the page.

The tire ring running north–south fixed north exactly for 2020, and the model now uses that one north for every year. The 2026 model was drawn separately, and next to two 2026 drone photos turned north-up it sits about 33° off (Chiba's long side, the container row and the trailer arc all agree), so the 2026 sun, shadows and sunset shots are off by that much.

worth answering first What changes if you answer: The sun, the shadows and the sunset camera shots for that year turn; nothing is rebuilt.

Q23

In 2024, was Chiba's front six rack bays wide (about 22 m, as the model has it) or seven bays (about 25.6 m)?

We rebuilt the 2024 front from your photo (vertical inset around the stairs, flaps leaning back on both sides), keeping the model's 6-bay width. But if the doors in the photo are ordinary 2 m doors and the landing sits at the upper floor, the whole front measures about 25–27 m wide, which is closer to 7 bays.

Your answer

improves fidelity What changes if you answer: If seven bays, Chiba 2024 grows by one bay (the flaps and the solarium get wider) in another reconstruction edit of the protected 2024 state; if six, nothing changes.

bay: one 12 ft (3.66 m) span of rack beams; the model's Chiba 2024 is 6 bays wide and 3 deep

Engineer's notes (not needed to answer)
(Parked; non-blocking. Added by W43.)

**What the engine sees.** `app/history/photographic-corrections.ts frontage2024` keeps the hall at 6 × 3 bays (21.95 m × 10.97 m).
Measured in the 1000 × 497 px photo: the facade spans x ≈ 25–978 px at the ground (953 px), so at the flap bottoms 6 bays gives
≈ 43.4 px/m. The door leaves are 70 px tall and the landing (the upper-floor level, 2.46–2.55 m in the model) is 88 px above
the ground, which gives ≈ 35–36 px/m at the inset. The flaps' outer edges converge by about 10 % from bottom to top, so the
camera is roughly 25 m away and the inset should read only about 10 % smaller than the flap bottoms (≈ 39 px/m), not 18 %.
With 6 bays the door would be about 1.8 m tall and the landing 2.2 m; with 7 bays they would be 2.1 m and 2.6 m. The lens and
the crop are unknown, so this does not settle it. **Default:** keep 6 bays.
**What the answer changes.** A 7-bay answer widens the hall frame, the decks and both flaps by one bay (a new
`reconstruction-edit` of `mars-2024`, HISTORY_IDS.md). Every Chiba 2024 hashed id then changes, and the pins stay.
